iris.nec.failure.title: [%s] Not Enough Crashes detected!
iris.nec.failure.description:
Not Enough Crashes can severely break the game while handling crashes, and does not provide accurate results.
A good alternative is MixinTrace, which can identify the cause of a crash more reliably and does not put the game in an invalid state.

options.iris.horizon.title: Horizon LOD Settings
options.iris.horizon.engine.tooltip: Use the experimental textured voxel LOD engine instead of the classic flat-color one. Distant terrain keeps real block textures and biome tint. Applied on world reload.
options.iris.horizon.enabled.tooltip: Renders explored terrain far beyond the server view distance using lightweight LOD meshes. Terrain is captured as you explore and persisted between sessions.
options.iris.horizon.shaders.tooltip: Keep rendering LOD terrain while a shader pack is active (flat-shaded). Disable if a specific pack misbehaves.
options.iris.horizon.distance.tooltip: Maximum LOD render distance, in chunks. Only terrain you have already explored can be shown.
options.iris.horizon.baseScale.tooltip: Blocks per LOD cell in the nearest detail ring (rounded down to a power of two). Lower = sharper, heavier.
options.iris.horizon.ringWidth.tooltip: Width of each detail ring in blocks. Past each ring the LOD cell size doubles, halving geometry density.
options.iris.horizon.uploads.tooltip: How many freshly built LOD meshes may be uploaded to the GPU per frame. Lower values smooth out frame pacing while exploring.
options.iris.horizon.saveInterval.toolti: Seconds between automatic saves of captured terrain data to disk.
options.iris.horizon.texturedLodUnderSha: Draw distant terrain through the shaderpack's own terrain program so it shows real block textures. Packs that support Distant Horizons normally draw distant terrain in flat colour, because those programs never sample a texture; turning this on trades that pack-specific handling — its own distant fog and material effects — for texture detail. Packs without Distant Horizons support always use this path.
options.iris.horizon.lodAutoClean.toolti: When the disk budget is reached, delete the cached LOD regions farthest from you instead of refusing to store more. Nearby terrain is kept; the far edge of old trips goes first. Off means the budget simply stops new terrain being stored.
options.iris.horizon.lodClear.tooltip: Delete this world's entire LOD cache. Requires Confirm Clear to be ticked as well; both are cleared again once it runs.
options.iris.horizon.lodClearConfirm.too: Safety tick for Clear LOD Cache. Nothing is deleted unless both are ticked when you apply — the cache can only be rebuilt by exploring or generating again.
options.iris.horizon.serverLodDisk.toolt: How much disk this world may use for LOD downloaded from a server. Nothing is deleted when the budget is reached: the client simply stops accepting more, so distant terrain stops filling in, and you are told in chat. Raise it for a large pre-generated server — a 4 km world is roughly 900 MB.
options.iris.horizon.threads.tooltip: Background threads used for LOD meshing and disk IO. Applied at game start.

options.iris.shadowDistance.enabled: Allows you to change the maximum distance for shadows. Terrain and entities beyond this distance will not cast shadows. Lowering the shadow distance can significantly increase performance.
options.iris.shadowDistance.disabled: Your current shader pack has already set a render distance for shadows; you cannot change it.
options.iris.shadowDistance.sodium_toolt: The shadow render distance controls how far away terrain can potentially be rendered in the shadow pass. Lower distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates. This option cannot be changed on packs which explicitly specify a shadow render distance. The actual shadow render distance is capped by the View Distance setting.
options.iris.colorSpace.sodium_tooltip: The color space to transform the screen to. Works on top of shader packs. Use SRGB if unsure.
